title: Roasted Tomato Soup
description:
On my trips to the Middle East, we would usually fly through London, sometimes spending an extra day there on the way home for meetings or a little relaxation. We would always arrive very early in the morning and after getting our bags and checking in, etc., we would head to the Café Richoux, near Picadilly Square. And, I would always have this Roasted Tomato Soup, which was so wonderful and soothing.
I would also always have to have a “Welsh Rarebit,” sort of a grilled cheese sandwich. This was because it reminded me of my Mom’s admonition after one of my protestations about one thing or another, “There’s no such thing as a “yes, but,” there’s only a “Rarebit.” As a kid, I had no idea what that was, but I do now!
Similarly, I had no idea as a kid what a “syclonestrucket” was when my Mom used that term to describe my bedroom. Only later did I realize that she was saying that my room looked like a “cyclone had struck it.” Needless to say, understanding precisely or not, I cleaned the room.
My experience is not much unlike Mommy’s, when she once saw a sign on our hotel room door in New York, “fuhgettaboudit.” She tried to sound it out – fudge a ta boo dit – without remembering her Long Island upbringing – and accent – to come up with a good Mafia-sounding “forget about it.”
Well, we digress. With this soup, especially on one of those cold Winter days, you can forget about it, and bask in the luxuriant smooth-ness of these liquid roasted tomatoes – and maybe remember your own good stories.
ingredients: 3 cups chicken stock or low-sodium broth
directions: Roast tomatoes and garlic 1 hour, then cool in the pan on a rack. Peel garlic.
Meanwhile, cook the onion, oregano, and sugar in butter in a 6-to-8 quarter heavy pot over moderately low heat, stirring frequently, until the onion is softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the roasted tomatoes, garlic, and stock. Simmer, covered 20 minutes.
Puree the soup in batches in a blender (or use an immersion blender), being very careful when blending hot liquids.
Force the blended mixture through a sieve into a clean pot, discarding the solids.
Stir in cream and salt and pepper to taste and simmer 2 minutes.
Divide the soup among the bowls and float a toast, maybe with a little pesto on top, in the center of each.
One year for Christmas, we made this with toasts shaped like Christmas trees. With these shapes, the reddish soup, and the green pesto topping, it was the perfect combination of Christmas colors!
Put oven rack in middle position and preheat to 350 degrees.
Arrange tomatoes, cut sides up, in 1 layer in a large shallow baking pan and add garlic to the pan.
Drizzle tomatoes with oil and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
